mentions.name: Buffee
mentions.description: This is a minimal, fast, Vim-inspired text editor for the web, designed as an embeddable and hackable building block for custom IDEs rather than a VSCode-like IDE. It ships at 2kb, smoothly handles 50+ million line files (1 billion lines with the high-capacity extension), and can function as a TUI or terminal on the web since its core efficiently renders plaintext in a fixed-width grid. There are no default key handlers; clients bring their own modes and controllers (e.g., modal editing, mouse selection, hot keys) via the extension system.
mentions.problem: The author felt the web IDE space was uninspired, with apps built around VSCode/Monaco effectively being hosted VSCode instances with a pre-installed extension and config.json.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Vim-inspired, as in it's minimal and fast, text editor on the web. No modal-editing yet but, once the current natural input mode is decoupled, clients can bring their own modes/controllers via the extension system.

It's meant to be embeddable and hackable, serving as a building block for custom IDEs as opposed to being IDE-like VSCode.
